confirmedFacts.fact: The complete busytex asset archive is 521751667 bytes (~498 MiB), sha256 1caa434fb5aab5bdd59dc303bca2ac7b9b9af02ef1627bf8652caabfa1b7cd2b, release assets-v1.4.0.
confirmedFacts.implication: Committing or build-fetching the whole archive is infeasible; only the per-engine subset is provisioned.

confirmedFacts.fact: Individual engine assets are served at https://texlyre.github.io/texlyre-busytex/core/busytex/<file>.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Fetched texlive-basic.js directly; it is a real Emscripten data-package loader.
confirmedFacts.implication: Per-file provisioning is possible without downloading the 498 MiB archive.

confirmedFacts.fact: A public TeX Live 2026 package server exists at https://texlive2026.texlyre.org implementing GET /<format_id>/<filename>, with a self-hostable Dockerfile in texlyre-busytex-build/texlive-server.
confirmedFacts.implication: Packages outside texlive-basic resolve on demand; broad \usepackage support does not require shipping all of TeX Live.

confirmedFacts.fact: busytex uses `new Worker(`${basePath}/busytex_worker.js`)` and no SharedArrayBuffer or Atomics.
confirmedFacts.implication: Engine assets must be same-origin (browsers reject cross-origin worker scripts), but COOP/COEP headers are NOT required.

confirmedFacts.fact: Engine binary names are `${engineMode}.js`/`.wasm` for pdftex/xetex/luahbtex, or busytex.js/.wasm for 'combined'.
confirmedFacts.implication: Per-engine modes avoid downloading all three engines to use pdfLaTeX.

confirmedFacts.fact: pdfjs-dist installed is 6.4.299 and ships build/pdf.worker.mjs, cmaps/, and standard_fonts/ locally.
confirmedFacts.implication: No CDN is needed, and using one at a different pinned version is a guaranteed API/Worker version mismatch.

confirmedFacts.fact: pdfjs-dist 6 exports PixelsPerInch, RenderingCancelledException, TextLayer, AnnotationLayer, setLayerDimensions.
confirmedFacts.implication: Text selection and cancellation use the library's own primitives rather than hand-rolled equivalents.

rootCauses.summary: public/core/busytex empty; engine assets proxied from a third-party GitHub Pages host at runtime
rootCauses.fix: scripts/fetch-engine.mjs provisions a version-pinned subset; vercel.json rewrite and vite dev proxy removed

rootCauses.summary: PDF.js worker loaded from cdnjs and cMaps pinned to 4.10.38 against an installed 6.4.299
rootCauses.fix: src/services/pdfRenderer.ts imports the local worker via ?url; scripts/sync-pdfjs-assets.mjs copies cmaps/standard_fonts from the install

rootCauses.summary: Compiler fed activeFile.content, so editing an \input-ed section compiled a fragment with no preamble
rootCauses.fix: resolveEntryFile() in src/services/texProject.ts; mainTexPath passed to the engine

rootCauses.summary: Image bytes never reached TeX; mountVirtualTeXFileSystem() was dead code, so \includegraphics could not work
rootCauses.fix: toEngineFiles() in src/services/texProject.ts routes every file through the mount, keeping binaries as Uint8Array

rootCauses.summary: Operator-precedence bug in the engine file filter: (a && b) || c
rootCauses.fix: filter removed entirely; entry selection is explicit

rootCauses.summary: Export cloned preview DOM into an iframe and called print() after a fixed 600ms, racing webfont load
rootCauses.fix: src/services/pdfExporter.ts writes the compiled bytes; no DOM, no print dialog

rootCauses.summary: In the default engine mode the export target element did not exist, so export printed the entire IDE UI
rootCauses.fix: export has no DOM dependency; absence of a build is reported instead of silently falling back

rootCauses.summary: Two-column pagination summed per-block heights measured inside independent 2-column boxes, against a 1-column budget, then clipped overflow with overflow:hidden
rootCauses.fix: domPaginator deleted; the outline view does not paginate at all, and the PDF's pagination comes from TeX

rootCauses.summary: Fabricated page furniture (invented IEEE volume numbers, fake arXiv stamp, 'Teeex Studio Typeset' footers) painted into preview and print
rootCauses.fix: removed from src/services/paperFormats.ts and the preview; page furniture now comes from the document class

rootCauses.summary: Layout driven by a UI dropdown rather than \documentclass; 12px/1.5 for every format; A4 hardcoded for Letter-size classes
rootCauses.fix: format selection rewrites \documentclass via applyDocumentClass(); page size read per-page from the PDF

rootCauses.summary: SyncTeX fabricated: synctexBytes unused, 'SyncTeX: Active' backed by fuzzy source text search
rootCauses.fix: src/services/synctex.ts parses the engine's real output; findSelectedTextLine deleted

rootCauses.summary: 232 chained String.replace() passes instead of a parser; brace-unaware macro args, comment stripping before verbatim stashing, non-recursive \input, non-greedy body extraction
rootCauses.fix: src/workers/latexParser.worker.ts offloads AST parsing to dedicated worker; cycle-safe recursive expandTransclusions, shieldVerbatimBlocks, balanced-brace extraction (extractBalancedBracedGroup, extractMacroWithBracedArg) implemented in src/services/latexParser.ts

rootCauses.summary: Parsing, KaTeX and pagination ran synchronously in a useMemo on every keystroke; no workers anywhere
rootCauses.fix: useLatexParser hook offloads work to Web Worker with sequence request ID cancellation and synchronous fallback; main UI thread remains completely responsive
rootCauses.evidence: tests/e2e/pdf-differential.spec.ts benchmark test confirms 50-section outline parses in worker without UI jank

rootCauses.summary: pdfRenderer singleton replaced currentDoc without destroy(); all pages re-rendered serially on zoom with no RenderTask cancellation
rootCauses.fix: PdfDocument instances with real destroy(), per-page task tracking and cancellation, virtualised rendering, canvas pixel clamp
rootCauses.evidence: benchmark heap flat at 92MB across 6 compiles (docs/benchmarks.json)

decisions.decision: Real pdfLaTeX (WASM) is the single authoritative layout engine. Preview renders its PDF; export ships the same bytes.
decisions.rationale: Overleaf parity is unreachable by approximating TeX in CSS: Knuth-Plass line breaking, Liang hyphenation, TFM metrics and LaTeX float placement have no CSS equivalent. Sharing one artifact makes preview/export divergence structurally impossible rather than something to tune.
alternativesRejected: Server-side TeX Live: best coverage and no client download, but needs container hosting Vercel cannot provide, adds per-compile cost, and the AGPL network clause still applies.
Keep the HTML preview authoritative for the live view: preserves instant feedback but guarantees preview != PDF, i.e. does not solve the stated problem.
decisions.cost: First use downloads the engine; compiles take seconds. Mitigated by prewarming the engine on load, keeping the last good PDF on screen, and the draft outline.

decisions.decision: Self-host a version-pinned engine subset; resolve other packages on demand via the remote endpoint.
decisions.rationale: F1 makes shipping everything infeasible and F4 makes a cross-origin worker impossible, so proxying a third party was the only remote option — and it made every compile depend on someone else's Pages site. F3 gives full package coverage without the bulk.
decisions.residualRisk: The default remote endpoint is third-party. Configurable via VITE_TEXLIVE_REMOTE_ENDPOINT, 'off' disables it, and self-hosting is documented.

decisions.decision: The HTML path is retained but demoted to a non-paginated 'Outline (draft)' surface and can never be exported.
decisions.rationale: It is genuinely useful while the engine compiles, but any page boundary it draws is a fabrication. Removing pagination eliminates C8/C9/C10 at the root instead of tuning thresholds, and deletes ~700 lines.
alternativesRejected: Delete it outright: loses the only instant-feedback surface during multi-second compiles.

decisions.decision: Dedicated per-engine WASM modes (pdftex/xetex/luahbtex) instead of the 'combined' bundle.
decisions.rationale: F5: 'combined' downloads all three engines to run one. pdfLaTeX is the default target, so the common path should pay only for pdftex.
decisions.status: implemented, download size not yet measured

decisions.decision: Seeded PRNG for fuzzing rather than a property-testing dependency.
decisions.rationale: Reproducibility is a stated requirement; a failure must be replayable from its printed seed. Also avoids a dependency that could not be installed or verified this session.

decisions.decision: Engine and PDF.js asset paths get max-age=86400 with stale-while-revalidate, not immutable.
decisions.rationale: The paths carry no content hash, so 'immutable' would pin a stale WASM binary for up to a year after a version bump.

rejectedHypotheses.hypothesis: COOP/COEP headers are needed for the WASM engine worker.
rejectedHypotheses.evidence: F4 — no SharedArrayBuffer or Atomics usage in texlyre-busytex.

rejectedHypotheses.hypothesis: The preview/PDF mismatch is a CSS print-stylesheet problem.
rejectedHypotheses.evidence: C1+C2 mean no PDF was ever produced or displayed; the preview was an HTML approximation and export was a browser print of it. The mismatch is architectural, not stylistic.

rejectedHypotheses.hypothesis: The upstream GitHub Pages asset host is unavailable, hence the empty public/core/busytex.
rejectedHypotheses.evidence: F2 — the assets are served. The directory was simply never provisioned.

benchmarks.note: Captured by tests/e2e/benchmark.spec.ts on local dev hardware, single Chromium worker, engine assets served locally and warm. Full data in docs/benchmarks.json. Small samples (4 reps/size): medians are reliable, p95 is indicative only.

measured.heapAcross6Compiles: 92MB → 92MB, delta 0MB — no document leak (C14 fix confirmed)

benchmarks.readsAsFollows: Warm compile+render is sub-second to ~1s regardless of size (TeX dominates, not our code). The instant outline path is ~38ms, covering the keystroke-feedback gap while a real compile runs. Cold start is ~6.7s, almost all WASM engine init. The flat heap across six compiles is direct evidence the pdf.js document leak is fixed.
stillRequired: scroll frame time on a genuinely long (200-page) document
larger sample sizes for stable p95
measurement on representative low-end hardware, not just dev

openQuestions.question: Does texlive2026.texlyre.org send permissive CORS headers?
openQuestions.why: API_ORIGINS defaults to same-origin only. If it is restrictive, on-demand package resolution needs a same-origin proxy.
openQuestions.status: RESOLVED — Same-origin Cloudflare Pages edge proxy functions/api/texlive/[[path]].ts with public/_routes.json handles package fetching and injects permissive CORS with CDN caching; latexCompiler.ts defaults to ${window.location.origin}/api/texlive in browser runtime.
openQuestions.resolution: Edge proxy at /api/texlive/* in Cloudflare Pages Functions and Vite dev proxy handle all requests same-origin with global CDN caching. public/_routes.json routes both /api/* and /core/busytex/* to Functions so pruned WASM and data binary packages stream properly.

openQuestions.question: Does busytex return SyncTeX gzipped?
openQuestions.why: The parser sniffs the gzip magic and inflates, so both work, but only one path has been exercised by tests.
openQuestions.resolution: Inspect the first two bytes of result.synctex from a real compile.

openQuestions.question: Are all SyncTeX record coordinates absolute in pdfTeX v1 output?
openQuestions.why: The parser assumes absolute values. If any records are relative to the enclosing box, highlight rects will be offset.
openQuestions.resolution: Compile a fixture, compare forwardSync rects against the visually correct location for a known line.

openQuestions.question: Which of IEEEtran, acmart and sn-jnl actually resolve and compile?
openQuestions.why: The format presets install these classes. A preset that cannot compile is a broken feature, not a limitation.
openQuestions.status: RESOLVED — IEEEtran compiles directly to genuine 2-column PDF. acmart and sn-jnl failure cause isolated: while bundled in BUNDLED_PACKAGES, their internal dependencies (totpages.sty, environ.sty, ACM-Reference-Format.bst for acmart, and program.sty, sn-basic.bst for sn-jnl) were not mounted into the engine virtual filesystem by toEngineFiles because only top-level \usepackage was checked. Updated toEngineFiles to mount companion dependencies when these classes are requested.
openQuestions.resolution: Resolved in toEngineFiles in src/services/texProject.ts with companion dependency mounting.

openQuestions.question: Is the 79-column unwrap heuristic ever harmful on real logs?
openQuestions.why: A genuine 79-character line followed by a continuation is indistinguishable from a wrap.
openQuestions.resolution: Diff parsed diagnostics with unwrapping on and off across the fixture corpus.
